question: In which year did the Indian state of Rajasthan get India’s first Panchayati Raj system?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1959.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **The Panchayati Raj system is a decentralized form of governance that aims to involve local communities in decision-making processes.**
 
• It was first introduced in India through the 73rd Amendment Act of 1992, which made it mandatory for all states to establish Panchayati Raj institutions.
 
• However, the first Panchayati Raj system in India was actually implemented in the state of Rajasthan in 1959, almost three decades before the constitutional amendment.
 
• The system was introduced by the then Chief Minister of Rajasthan, Mohan Lal Sukhadia, as a way to empower rural communities and promote local self-governance.
 
• The Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Act of 1959 established a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj institutions at the village, block, and district levels.
 
• **The institutions were given powers and functions related to local development planning, resource mobilization, and service delivery.**
 
• The success of the Rajasthan Panchayati Raj system inspired other states to adopt similar models of decentralization.
 
• **Today, Panchayati Raj institutions exist in all states of India and play a crucial role in grassroots democracy and development.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In rural India, the Panchayati Raj system governs villages locally.
 
• Their duties include "economic development, strengthening social justice and implementation of Central and State Government Schemes including those 29 subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule."
 
• The provision of the Indian Constitution that deals with panchayats is called Part IX.
 
• It adds that there are three PRI levels in states or Union Territories with populations greater than two million.
 
 
• **the village-level gram panchayats.**
 
• **the block-level panchayat samiti, also known as the block samiti or mandal parishad.**
 
• **the district panchayat, or district council, at the local level.**
